brief.title: Driver Dispatch & Proof-of-Delivery Platform
business_goals: Reduce manual dispatch effort and improve operational efficiency.
Minimize 'item not received' disputes and associated chargebacks.
Ensure reliable proof of delivery for every order.
Optimize rider utilization by considering both distance and current workload.
Improve delivery success rates for failed deliveries through automated reattempts.
Enhance real-time visibility of rider location and prevent unauthorized detours.
Be prepared for increased delivery volumes during peak sale events.
Streamline the customer experience for proof of delivery.

stakeholders.name: Karan Malhotra
concerns: Manual dispatch inefficiency for 3,500 daily deliveries (220 riders).
Need for auto-assignment of nearest available rider.
Criticality of proof of delivery (photo, signature/OTP) to reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks.
Integration with existing Unicommerce order management system.
Preventing riders from going off-route unnoticed.
Project deadline before the next big sale event (approx. 10 weeks out).
Budget cap of 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.

stakeholders.name: Neha Iyer
concerns: Auto-assignment logic must consider both distance and current rider load.
Automated OTP delivery to customers via SMS when rider is near drop location.
Scope management, specifically excluding batch route optimization for this phase.

stakeholders.name: Ravi Kumar
concerns: Rider mobile app functionality (route display, offline capability for patchy network).
Rider device compatibility (app must run acceptably on low-end Android devices, as riders use their own phones).

stakeholders.name: Sameer Qureshi
concerns: Live tracking updates for customer-facing link (at least every 30 seconds).
Utilizing existing Google Maps Platform contract for maps and routing.
Scalability of dispatch engine to assign riders within 10 seconds at peak (9,000 deliveries/day).

constraints: Budget capped at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.
Project must be live before the next big sale event (approximately 10 weeks out).
Must integrate with the existing Unicommerce order management system; Unicommerce will not be replaced.
Maps and routing must use the existing Google Maps Platform contract.
Rider mobile app must function acceptably on low-end Android devices.
Rider mobile app must work with patchy network connectivity, queuing updates offline and syncing when signal returns.
Dispatch engine must assign a rider within 10 seconds, even at peak volumes (9,000 deliveries/day).
Customer-facing tracking link needs to update rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
out_of_scope: Route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries (batch routing).
Replacing the existing Unicommerce order management system.
open_questions: What is the precise date of the 'next big sale event'?
What are the specific requirements for photo proof of delivery (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, quality standards)?
What are the exact requirements for signature proof of delivery (e.g., digital signature pad, finger signature on screen)?
How will the system handle cases where OTP delivery fails or the customer does not have a phone?
What are the specific metrics for 'acceptably' running on low-end Android devices (e.g., minimum OS version, RAM, storage)?
Are there any specific security or privacy regulations related to customer data (OTP, location, photos) that need to be adhered to?

requirements.statement: The system shall auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.
requirements.evidence: we need the system to auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.

requirements.statement: The system's auto-assignment logic shall consider the distance to the rider.
requirements.evidence: The auto-assignment needs to consider both distance

requirements.statement: The system's auto-assignment logic shall consider the current rider load.
requirements.evidence: and current rider load — someone with three pending drops shouldn't get a fourth if there's a free rider two streets away.

requirements.statement: The rider mobile application shall display the rider's route for the day.
requirements.evidence: Riders need a mobile app that shows their route for the day

requirements.statement: The rider mobile application shall function with patchy network connectivity.
requirements.evidence: and it must work with patchy network — a lot of our delivery zones have poor connectivity.

requirements.statement: The rider mobile application shall queue updates offline and sync them when network signal returns.
requirements.evidence: The app should queue updates offline and sync when signal comes back.

requirements.statement: The system shall support photo proof of delivery for every delivery.
requirements.rationale: To reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks.
requirements.evidence: every delivery needs a photo

requirements.statement: The system shall support signature proof of delivery for every delivery.
requirements.rationale: To reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks.
requirements.evidence: and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete.

requirements.statement: The system shall support OTP proof of delivery for every delivery.
requirements.rationale: To reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks.
requirements.evidence: and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete.

requirements.statement: The system shall require either a photo, signature, or OTP to mark a delivery as complete.
requirements.rationale: To reduce 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks.
requirements.evidence: every delivery needs a photo and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete.

requirements.statement: The system should automatically send an OTP to the customer via SMS when the rider is within a defined proximity of the drop location.
requirements.evidence: Ideally the OTP should be sent to the customer automatically via SMS when the rider is within, say, 500 meters of the drop location.

requirements.statement: The customer-facing tracking link shall update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
requirements.evidence: the customer-facing tracking link needs to update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds.

requirements.statement: The system shall utilize the existing Google Maps Platform contract for maps and routing.
requirements.evidence: Our maps and routing run on the Google Maps Platform, that's already contracted.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow riders to select a reason code for failed deliveries.
requirements.evidence: Failed deliveries need a reason code — customer not available, wrong address, refused

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically trigger a reattempt for failed deliveries on the next day.
requirements.evidence: and those should automatically trigger a reattempt the next day

requirements.statement: The system shall limit reattempts for a failed delivery to a maximum of two attempts before returning to the hub.
requirements.evidence: up to two attempts before we return it to the hub.

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with the existing Unicommerce order management system.
requirements.evidence: We also need this to integrate with our existing order management system, Unicommerce

requirements.statement: The system shall send real-time order status updates to Unicommerce.
requirements.evidence: so that order status updates flow back there in real time.

requirements.statement: The dispatch engine shall assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at peak volumes of 9,000 deliveries per day.
requirements.evidence: The dispatch engine has to assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at that peak.

requirements.statement: The system shall not include batch route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries in this phase.
requirements.evidence: Route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries — like solving the best order to visit 40 stops — is out of scope for this phase.

requirements.statement: The rider mobile application shall run acceptably on low-end Android devices.
requirements.evidence: the app has to run acceptably on low-end Android, we can't assume everyone has a flagship phone.

requirements.statement: The system shall detect when a rider goes off-route.
requirements.evidence: Last month we had a rider go completely off-route for two hours and nobody noticed until the customer called to complain, that shouldn't be able to happen again.

epics.title: Automated Dispatch & Route Optimization
epics.goal: To efficiently assign deliveries to riders and provide clear routes, optimizing utilization and ensuring timely deliveries.

epics.title: Secure Proof of Delivery
epics.goal: To provide multiple secure methods for proof of delivery, reducing disputes and ensuring delivery confirmation.

epics.title: Failed Delivery Management
epics.goal: To streamline the process for handling failed deliveries and improve success rates through automated reattempts.

epics.title: Core Platform Integrations & Resilience
epics.goal: To ensure seamless integration with existing systems and provide a robust, performant rider application that functions reliably under varying conditions.

stories.title: Auto-assign orders considering nearest rider and workload
stories.i_want: the system to auto-assign orders to the nearest available rider, considering their current workload
stories.so_that: deliveries are efficiently distributed, reducing manual effort and optimizing rider utilization

acceptance_criteria.given: an unassigned order and multiple available riders with known locations and current loads
acceptance_criteria.when: a new order is received
acceptance_criteria.then: the system identifies the rider who is nearest and has the lightest current load.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider has been identified as the optimal choice
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to assign the order
acceptance_criteria.then: the order is assigned to that rider and their workload is updated.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is already at maximum capacity
acceptance_criteria.when: a new order is received
acceptance_criteria.then: the system does not assign the order to that rider, even if they are the nearest.

stories.title: Consider rider distance in auto-assignment
stories.i_want: the auto-assignment logic to consider the distance to the rider
stories.so_that: deliveries are assigned efficiently based on proximity

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple available riders
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates rider proximity for an order
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider's current location is used to determine distance to the pickup point

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple available riders at different distances
acceptance_criteria.when: the system performs auto-assignment
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider with the shortest distance to the pickup point is prioritized

stories.title: Consider rider workload in auto-assignment
stories.i_want: the auto-assignment logic to consider the current rider load
stories.so_that: deliveries are distributed fairly and riders are not overloaded

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple available riders
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates rider availability for an order
acceptance_criteria.then: the number of active deliveries assigned to each rider is factored in

acceptance_criteria.given: two riders with similar proximity but different workloads
acceptance_criteria.when: the system performs auto-assignment
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider with the lower current load is prioritized

stories.title: Display daily route in rider app
stories.i_want: my mobile application to display my route for the day
stories.so_that: I can efficiently plan my deliveries and navigate effectively

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider has assigned deliveries for the day
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider opens the mobile application
acceptance_criteria.then: a clear, optimized route showing all delivery stops is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is on a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider views the route
acceptance_criteria.then: the current location and next stop are highlighted

stories.title: Real-time customer tracking link
stories.i_want: my tracking link to update the rider's location frequently
stories.so_that: I have real-time visibility of my delivery status

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is viewing their tracking link
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider's location changes
acceptance_criteria.then: the map on the tracking link updates the rider's position within 30 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is en route
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer refreshes the tracking link
acceptance_criteria.then: the displayed rider location is current within 30 seconds

stories.title: Integrate with Google Maps Platform for routing
stories.i_want: the system to utilize the existing Google Maps Platform contract for maps and routing
stories.so_that: we leverage our current investment and ensure consistent mapping services

acceptance_criteria.given: a new order is assigned
acceptance_criteria.when: the system generates a route for the rider
acceptance_criteria.then: the route calculation is performed using the Google Maps Platform API

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider's location needs to be displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: the system renders a map
acceptance_criteria.then: the map is sourced from the Google Maps Platform

stories.title: Optimize dispatch engine for peak volume assignment speed
stories.i_want: the dispatch engine to assign riders within 10 seconds, even during peak volumes
stories.so_that: orders are processed without delay during busy periods, ensuring timely deliveries

acceptance_criteria.given: 9,000 orders are processed within a day
acceptance_criteria.when: a new order comes in
acceptance_criteria.then: a rider is assigned to that order within 10 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: the system is under peak load (e.g., 9,000 orders/day simulation)
acceptance_criteria.when: a rider becomes available
acceptance_criteria.then: the system assigns a new order to them within 10 seconds

stories.notes: This story focuses on optimizing the performance of the core dispatch logic (S-001, not in this list) to meet the specified SLA. It depends on S-001 being implemented.

stories.title: Off-route detection
stories.i_want: the system to detect when a rider goes off-route
stories.so_that: I can monitor rider adherence and prevent unauthorized detours

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is on an assigned route
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider deviates more than a predefined distance (e.g., 500m) from the planned route
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays the rider's status as "off-route" to the Dispatch Manager and logs the event.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is flagged as "off-route"
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider returns to the planned route
acceptance_criteria.then: the system updates the rider's status accordingly

stories.title: Photo proof of delivery
stories.i_want: to be able to capture a photo as proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can confirm successful delivery and minimize disputes

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is at the delivery location
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider mobile application displays a 'Take Photo' button or icon.

acceptance_criteria.given: a photo is taken
acceptance_criteria.when: the delivery is marked complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the photo is stored and linked to the delivery record

stories.title: Signature proof of delivery
stories.i_want: to be able to capture a customer's signature as proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can confirm successful delivery and minimize disputes

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is at the delivery location
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider mobile application displays a signature capture interface.

acceptance_criteria.given: a signature is captured
acceptance_criteria.when: the delivery is marked complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the signature is stored and linked to the delivery record

stories.title: OTP proof of delivery
stories.i_want: to be able to collect an OTP from the customer as proof of delivery
stories.so_that: I can confirm successful delivery with an additional layer of security

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is at the delivery location
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider mobile application displays an OTP input field.

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid OTP is entered
acceptance_criteria.when: the delivery is marked complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the OTP validation status is recorded with the delivery

stories.title: Mandatory proof of delivery
stories.i_want: the system to require at least one form of proof (photo, signature, or OTP) to mark a delivery as complete
stories.so_that: every delivery has verifiable confirmation

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is at the delivery location
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete without providing any proof
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays an error message (e.g., 'Proof of Delivery Required') and prevents the delivery from being marked complete.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider has provided either a photo, signature, or valid OTP
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark a delivery as complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the system successfully marks the delivery as complete and records the chosen proof type.

stories.notes: This story depends on the implementation of Photo (S-009), Signature (S-010), and OTP (S-011) proof mechanisms (not in this list).

stories.title: Auto-send OTP to customer
stories.i_want: the system to automatically send an OTP to my phone via SMS when the rider is nearby
stories.so_that: I am prepared for the delivery and the OTP process is streamlined

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is assigned to a delivery
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider enters a predefined proximity (e.g., 500m) to the drop location
acceptance_criteria.then: an SMS containing an OTP is automatically sent to the customer's registered mobile number

acceptance_criteria.given: an OTP has been sent
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider moves out of proximity and then re-enters
acceptance_criteria.then: a new OTP is not sent unless the previous one has expired or the delivery status has changed

stories.title: Rider selects reason for failed delivery
stories.i_want: to be able to select a reason code for failed deliveries
stories.so_that: the system accurately records why a delivery could not be completed

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery cannot be completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark it as failed
acceptance_criteria.then: the rider mobile application presents a predefined list of reason codes (e.g., "Customer not available", "Address incorrect")

acceptance_criteria.given: a reason code is selected
acceptance_criteria.when: the delivery is marked as failed
acceptance_criteria.then: the selected reason code is stored with the delivery record

stories.title: Automate reattempts for failed deliveries
stories.i_want: the system to automatically trigger a reattempt for failed deliveries on the next day
stories.so_that: delivery success rates improve by ensuring a second chance for missed deliveries

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery is marked as failed today (first attempt)
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes end-of-day tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: a new delivery attempt is scheduled for the next day

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery is scheduled for reattempt
acceptance_criteria.when: the system assigns deliveries for the next day
acceptance_criteria.then: the reattempted delivery appears in the assigned rider's manifest.

stories.notes: This story depends on the ability to mark a delivery as failed (R-014, not in this list) and the core auto-assignment logic (S-001, not in this list) for re-assignment.

stories.title: Limit reattempts for failed deliveries
stories.i_want: the system to limit reattempts for a failed delivery to a maximum of two attempts before returning to the hub
stories.so_that: resources are not wasted on endlessly attempting undeliverable orders and items are returned efficiently

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery has failed once
acceptance_criteria.when: a reattempt is scheduled
acceptance_criteria.then: the system increments the attempt count for that delivery to one

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery has failed two times
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes end-of-day tasks after the second failure
acceptance_criteria.then: the delivery is marked for return to hub, and no further reattempts are scheduled.

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery is marked for return to hub
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider views their manifest
acceptance_criteria.then: the item is listed as "Return to Hub".

stories.notes: This story depends on the mechanism for triggering reattempts (S-015).

stories.title: Rider app offline functionality
stories.i_want: my mobile application to function even with patchy network connectivity
stories.so_that: I can continue my work without interruption in areas with poor signal

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider is on a route with no network connectivity
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider views their assigned deliveries
acceptance_criteria.then: the delivery list and details are accessible

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider completes a delivery offline
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider attempts to mark it complete
acceptance_criteria.then: the action is recorded locally without immediate network access

stories.title: Rider app offline capability and data synchronization
stories.i_want: my mobile application to function and queue updates when offline, and sync them when network returns
stories.so_that: I can continue my work without interruption in areas with patchy network, and all my delivery actions are eventually recorded accurately

acceptance_criteria.given: the rider mobile application is running and network connectivity is lost
acceptance_criteria.when: the rider performs actions (e.g., marks delivery complete, captures proof)
acceptance_criteria.then: the application remains responsive, and actions are queued locally.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rider has queued delivery updates while offline
acceptance_criteria.when: network connectivity is restored
acceptance_criteria.then: all queued delivery updates are automatically sent to the server.

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery update is sent after being queued offline
acceptance_criteria.when: the server receives the update
acceptance_criteria.then: the delivery status is accurately reflected in the system.

stories.title: Integrate with Unicommerce OMS for order ingestion
stories.i_want: the system to integrate with the existing Unicommerce order management system
stories.so_that: new orders are automatically ingested without manual data entry

acceptance_criteria.given: a new order is created in Unicommerce
acceptance_criteria.when: the integration runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the order details are successfully imported into the dispatch platform

acceptance_criteria.given: an order is imported
acceptance_criteria.when: the order details are viewed in the dispatch platform
acceptance_criteria.then: the imported order details are displayed accurately in the dispatch platform's order list.

stories.notes: This story covers the initial integration for basic order ingestion. Further breakdown might be needed for complex edge cases or specific data fields if they emerge.

stories.title: Send real-time order status to Unicommerce
stories.i_want: the system to send real-time order status updates to Unicommerce
stories.so_that: the OMS always has the most current information about delivery progress

acceptance_criteria.given: a delivery status changes (e.g., "Assigned", "Out for Delivery", "Delivered")
acceptance_criteria.when: the status is updated in the dispatch platform
acceptance_criteria.then: the new status is sent to Unicommerce within 60 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: an order status update is sent to Unicommerce
acceptance_criteria.when: the status is checked in Unicommerce
acceptance_criteria.then: it reflects the latest status from the dispatch platform

stories.notes: This story depends on the successful integration with Unicommerce (S-019, not in this list) for order ingestion. It covers sending real-time updates for key status changes.

stories.title: Ensure acceptable rider app performance on low-end Android devices
stories.i_want: the mobile application to run acceptably on low-end Android devices
stories.so_that: all riders can use the application effectively regardless of their device model, without frustration or delays

acceptance_criteria.given: the rider mobile application is installed on a specified low-end Android device (e.g., 2GB RAM, Quad-core 1.5GHz CPU)
acceptance_criteria.when: the application is launched
acceptance_criteria.then: the application loads and is ready for interaction within 5 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: the rider mobile application is running on a specified low-end Android device
acceptance_criteria.when: navigating between any two primary screens (e.g., 'My Deliveries' to 'Delivery Details')
acceptance_criteria.then: screen transitions complete within 2 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: the rider mobile application is running on a specified low-end Android device
acceptance_criteria.when: performing a core action like marking a delivery complete or capturing proof
acceptance_criteria.then: the action processes and updates the UI without noticeable lag (e.g., within 1 second)

stories.notes: This story represents the effort to design, develop, and test the rider application to meet specific performance benchmarks on low-end hardware, rather than a post-development optimization phase.

gaps.description: The business goal 'Streamline the customer experience for proof of delivery' is not fully covered. While OTP delivery is mentioned, there are no explicit requirements or backlog items detailing how customers will access or view photo/signature proof of delivery.
gaps.suggested_question: How will customers access or view their proof of delivery (photo/signature) after a successful delivery? Is there a specific customer-facing interface planned for this, beyond the real-time tracking link?

gaps.description: The precise date for the 'next big sale event' is unknown, making the project deadline (R-023) difficult to plan against.
gaps.suggested_question: What is the precise date of the 'next big sale event' that the project must be live before?

gaps.description: Specific requirements for photo proof of delivery (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, quality standards) are not detailed.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the specific requirements for photo proof of delivery, such as mandatory timestamp, geotagging, or minimum image quality standards?

gaps.description: Exact requirements for signature proof of delivery (e.g., digital signature pad, finger signature on screen) are not detailed.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the exact requirements for signature proof of delivery, such as whether it needs to support a digital signature pad or finger signature on screen?

gaps.description: The process for handling failed OTP delivery or situations where a customer does not have a phone is not explicitly defined, despite R-010 allowing alternatives.
gaps.suggested_question: What is the fallback process if OTP delivery fails or the customer does not have a phone to receive the OTP? Should the rider default to photo or signature POD in such cases?

gaps.description: The specific metrics for 'acceptably' running on low-end Android devices are not defined.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the specific metrics or minimum specifications for 'acceptably' running on low-end Android devices (e.g., minimum OS version, RAM, storage, performance benchmarks)?

gaps.description: There are no requirements or backlog items addressing specific security or privacy regulations related to customer data (OTP, location, photos).
gaps.suggested_question: Are there any specific security or privacy regulations (e.g., data retention, encryption, access controls) that need to be adhered to for customer data such as OTPs, location information, or proof of delivery photos?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog demonstrates strong coverage of most business goals and stakeholder concerns, particularly for auto-assignment, proof of delivery mechanisms, failed delivery processes, and real-time tracking. Key non-functional requirements like performance, scalability, and integration are also well-addressed. However, several ambiguities exist regarding the precise details of proof of delivery, fallback mechanisms for OTP, and specific performance metrics for the rider application. Critically, there is a high-severity gap concerning the lack of requirements for security and privacy regulations related to customer data, and the exact project deadline remains undefined, posing a risk to project planning.
